plugins.name: agentz-publisher
plugins.description: Guides contributors through publishing to the agentz marketplace in four phases: Analyse the idea, Research the catalog for duplicates, Build with HVE Core, and Validate with evals before opening a pull request.

skills.name: analyse-request
skills.description: Analyse what someone wants to publish to the agentz marketplace and capture it as an intent brief before anything is built. Use when someone says "I want to publish an agent", "I have an idea for a skill", "can we share this prompt with other teams", or starts the agentz publishing flow. This is phase 1 of 4 (Analyse, Research, Build, Validate). Do not use to build or edit files, or for plugins that already exist.

skills.name: build-plugin
skills.description: Build a new agentz marketplace plugin from a confirmed intent brief, scaffolding the classic plugin layout and authoring its skill, using HVE Core's hve-builder where it is supported, or the built-in checklist everywhere else. Use when the user says "create a plugin", "new plugin", "scaffold a skill for the marketplace", or after research-catalog returns a "new" verdict. This is phase 3 of 4 (Analyse, Research, Build, Validate). Do not use to edit an existing plugin's logic or to install plugins.

skills.name: research-catalog
skills.description: Search the agentz marketplace catalog for plugins, skills, agents and commands that already do what a new one would, and return a reuse, extend or new verdict. Use when someone asks "does agentz already have", "is there a skill for", or plans a new agent, skill or plugin. Use during research, including with rpi-research, and before hve-builder creates an artifact for agentz. This is phase 2 of 4 (Analyse, Research, Build, Validate). Do not use to build anything or to review an open pull request.

skills.name: validate-plugin
skills.description: Validate a new or changed agentz plugin before publishing by writing its Vally evals, running them, running the marketplace gate locally, and producing a publish-readiness report. Use when the user says "validate my plugin", "write evals for this skill", "is my plugin ready to publish", or after build-plugin finishes. This is phase 4 of 4 (Analyse, Research, Build, Validate). Do not use to review someone else's pull request.

agents.name: publisher
agents.description: Guides someone through publishing an agent, skill or plugin to the agentz marketplace in four phases (Analyse, Research, Build, Validate). Use when someone wants to publish or share an agent or skill with other teams. Delegates each phase to its agentz-publisher skill.

commands.name: new-plugin
commands.description: Publish a new agent, skill or plugin to the agentz marketplace (Analyse, Research, Build, Validate)

plugins.name: bicep-avm-review
plugins.description: Reviews Bicep templates against Azure Verified Modules (AVM) and organisation conventions, and produces a traceable findings report.

skills.name: bicep-avm-review
skills.description: Review Azure Bicep templates and parameter files against Azure Verified Modules (AVM) and organisation IaC conventions, and produce a findings report with evidence. Use when the user asks to "review my Bicep", "check this against AVM", "is this template production ready", "audit our IaC", or opens a PR that changes *.bicep or *.bicepparam files. Do not use for Terraform, ARM JSON authoring, or for deploying resources.

agents.name: iac-reviewer
agents.description: Read-only reviewer for infrastructure-as-code pull requests. Use when asked to review a PR or branch that changes Bicep. Delegates the review logic to the bicep-avm-review skill.

plugins.name: bicep-writer
plugins.description: Writes new Azure Bicep templates composed from Azure Verified Modules (AVM), with pinned module versions, secure defaults and local compile checks.

skills.name: bicep-writer
skills.description: Write new Azure Bicep templates and .bicepparam files composed from Azure Verified Modules (AVM), with pinned module versions, secure defaults and a local compile check. Use when the user asks to "write Bicep for", "create a Bicep template", "generate Azure IaC in Bicep", or "add an AVM module to this template". Do not use for reviewing or auditing existing Bicep, for Terraform, Pulumi or raw ARM JSON authoring, or for deploying resources to Azure.

plugins.name: cloud-avengers
plugins.description: AI-assisted AWS to Azure migration factory. Provides 10 specialist agents and 22 skills that orchestrate the full migration pipeline: AWS discovery → Azure architecture design → IaC transformation → code refactor → CI/CD pipeline build → deployment → validation.

plugins.name: onboarding
plugins.description: Sets up marketplace contributors, and publishes plugin repos to the marketplace through pull requests

skills.name: contributor-conventions
skills.description: The agentz rules for creating or editing plugin content under plugins/ - folder layout, skill, agent and command conventions, Vally eval rules and the commands to run after a change. Use when someone creates or changes a skill, agent, command, manifest or eval in agentz, asks where a plugin file goes, how to write evals, or what the CI gate requires. Do not use to set up a machine (use setup-machine), to run the publishing flow (use agentz-publisher) or to install plugins for normal use.

skills.name: setup-machine
skills.description: Set up this machine to contribute plugins to the agentz marketplace. Installs agentz-publisher, HVE Core as a plugin where supported, Python with PyYAML and Vally for evals. Use when someone wants contributor machine setup or has just installed onboarding. Do not use for automatic source-repository sync (use sync-marketplace), plugin use, or unrelated tools.

skills.name: sync-marketplace
skills.description: Add a GitHub Actions workflow to a source repo that already contains a plugin, so each new plugin version is published to the agentz marketplace as a linked plugin through a draft pull request. Use when someone asks to sync, publish or keep a plugin from their own repo up to date in the marketplace. Do not use for ordinary machine setup, installing plugins, building a new plugin from loose artifacts, or reviewing a pull request.

commands.name: init
commands.description: Set up marketplace contribution tools, or set up a plugin repo to publish to the marketplace
